I found the relevant code. The fix belongs in the `split_by_string_creator` lambda in `TokenizerFactory.cpp`, which currently rejects only an empty array but not empty-string elements.

The change is complete. The `splitByString` tokenizer creator now validates each separator element and rejects the query with a `BAD_ARGUMENTS` error if any element is an empty string, regardless of its position in the array.

The fix in `src/Interpreters/TokenizerFactory.cpp`:
- Iterates over every separator in the array (as before)
- Now checks each one: if `separator.empty()`, it throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS` immediately

This handles all the required cases:
- `['']` → rejected (single empty string)
- `[' ', '']` → rejected (empty string alongside a valid separator)
- Any other position of the empty string → rejected, since the check runs on every element during iteration.

The existing "separators cannot be empty" check (for a completely empty array `[]`) is preserved.
